briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and DeepSeek R2 escalate frontier race as compute shortages intensify global tensions

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI race has accelerated with multiple frontier labs releasing advanced models this month. US-China chip restrictions continue to reshape alliances while safety concerns mount around deployment at scale.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI launched o4 with enhanced multi-agent reasoning. Anthropic's Claude 4.5 and Google's Gemini 3 show gains in long-context tasks. Meta open-sourced Llama 4 while xAI and DeepSeek released competitive alternatives.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level with applications in multi-agent, automotive, and IoT environments.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA reported record Blackwell demand while TSMC ramps 2nm production. Microsoft and Google announced new $5B+ data center clusters in Texas and Arizona amid power constraints.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will the first AGI system emerge from a US lab or a Chinese state-backed consortium by 2028?
